I am sorry but watches are not that common here. Time has little meaning in this quite boring colony.
There is so much left that still needs to be discovered in this world.
The Thaian monarch entrusted Venore with much responsibility to manage this colony. Sadly he did not entrust the entire control in our hands which is a constant reason for all kinds of problems.
Those animals are one of the worst things we have to face here.
There must be some way to leverage their hatred towards those apes.
Luckily, this horrible ugly things stay in their own territory but who knows for how long? We should never show them any sign of weakness.
A somewhat chaotic town. I understand how its growth dictated the shape of its community but I also see the flaws in the outcome.
Venore is a beautiful city and its community is built up on commerce. Therefore it serves the needs of everyone who wants to contribute his share to the welfare of the city.

Another area that could and should prosper under Venoran guidance. If the king sees how we handle this settlement, he will for sure be impressed enough to allow us more freedom on that promising isle.
Their independence is just insane viewed from an economic angle. A complete waste of resources.
This continent is a challenge and an opportunity at the same time.
People there are somewhat strange. In my opinion their philosophy isn't good for business but the minds of people can be changed if you use the right arguments.
Well, I admit I fail to see any profit that could safely be made by trading with that city, but even unsafe profit is a good one. Prices have to be adjusted accordingly to the course.

Ah, home sweet home! Though I don't mind being here for a while, my heart still belongs to Kazordoon. ...
In a few decades, I'll certainly return there and hand over this tavern to someone else.
Every dwarf needs some relaxation now and then. This is the place where the miners come to share stories about home and hear news about the latest events like the giant beaver rodeos.
If you need to ask, you don't need to know.
The miners are a hardy folk. They love the mines, the sweat, the hammering of pick axes, and the smell of stone dust. And they love to curse about that all over a mug of beer. ...
That's their way to do it and you can't really understand it if you're not a miner yourself.
For all I've heard, the mines are growing at a steady pace and the construction is stable.

The cousin of my mother's neighbour knows someone who claims to have seen a strange guy in the Kazordoon tavern. He was wearing a dark cloak and beneath it he hid a weapon that might have been Excalibug.
If the orcs come here to kill us, we will be prepared! They will pay heavily for every attack.
Dragonkin! You can't expect anything good from dragons and the likes of them.
It wouldn't surprise me if there were another minotaur city somewhere on this continent. They are a pest.
Yeah, another land where Thais tries to get a foot in the door. I really hope they don't get us into a war or something.

Their representative never comes here for a drink. It seems he's afraid that something might slip him when he is drunk.
Now come on, this is more of a city than a cave by now. You have shops, a depot, a bank and even a tavern! Sunlight isn't that healthy anyway.
Those mages don't support us much with our project. I think everything they did was sending us this trader for magic stuff that no one but a few adventurers needs anyway. ...
I think he's quite at a loss on how to handle the situation down here, but who cares? That's his problem, not ours.
Take a look, but not a sip before you've paid. And I hope it stays like this and you don't get any strange ideas about rice.
He's a good man with a dwarven sense of humour. He is very popular among his men.
Ah the guild. Each year, back in Kazordoon, the most influential breweries compete to become the official beer supplier for the guild meetings. ...
Astonishingly, the guild needs less than a month to come up with a decision in this matter.
We've accomplished quite much since we started this base.
Bye.

Oh, I'm sorry, but I'm not interested in buying or selling anything.
I've been almost everywhere in Tibia.
I'm trying to explore each spot of Tibia, and one day I'll have seen it all.
A fine city, but the king has some problems enforcing the law.
King Tibianus is the ruler of Thais. The island of Rookgaard belongs to his kingdom.
It's a nice little island on which you can learn how to fight. I can see it in your eyes - you want to become a famous adventurer and explorer just like me!
I fought fierce monsters, climbed the highest mountains, explored the deepest dungeons and crossed the sea on a raft.
Oh, I fought orcs, cyclopses, minotaurs, even dragons, and many other creatures.
I don't like the way they look at you. Their eye seems to pierce right through you. Creepy!
They are nasty monsters, particularly as they have distance fighters and mages in their clans. My backpack is handmade from minotaur leather.
Their breath is so hot! I had to cut my hair after my last encounter with a dragon because the ends were all burnt. That's what you gotta deal with as a female adventurer!
Not the nicest guys you can encounter. I had some clashes with them and finally ended up being their prisoner for a few months.
I speak some Orcish words, not many though, just a few basics like 'yes' and 'no'.

I had no time to explore the dungeons of this isle yet, but I've seen two big caves in the East, and there is a ruined tower to the north-west. Oh, and there're the sewers.
I like sewers. I made my very first battle experience in the sewers below Thais. The small sewer system of Rookgaard has some nasty rats to fight.

An extraordinary warrior. He's the first and last line of defence of Rookgaard.

Sometimes I have the strong urge to use it to knock someone out.
You know, on mainland you will be able to cast magic spells which provide you with light. You won't really need torches anymore.
Spells are only taught in the guildhalls of the mainland.
The best weapons on this isle are just toothpicks compared with the weapons warriors wield on the mainland.
You'll be surprised once you leave this island. The world outside there is gigantic.
My voyage on the sea was exhausting. The weather was bad, the waves high and my raft quite simple. There's a certain excitement to it, though.
I left my raft at the south-eastern shore. I forgot my private notebook on it. If you could return it to me, I would be very grateful.

Sometimes those evil beings take the most naughty children to raise them as their own underwater.
Ah, there is little in the world that comes close to the taste of rum.
Sugar lets the money flow. We depend heavily on it.
Thais might be a splendid town, but this is of no use to us here. The situation in our town gets worse with every ship full of foreigners that arrives here.

I work here. Doin' the stuff that I'm ordered to.
So, you are looking for some kind of vehicle to ease travelling around these parts? Well then ...
One of the teams I was in, recently conducted some experiments concerning some kind of glider. We were tasked with the actual flight of the thing. ...
However, we could never quite get that thing to do what we asked it to. Still, a revolutionary thing - incredible, really. It was glooth powered but don't get your hopes up just yet. ...
The only thing left from this project, are blueprints. We never got it to actually lift off. I know of some guy who claimed to have found a way - but that one is not working with us anymore. ...
If I remember correctly, his name was professor Pierre Zeronex. But beware, that guy can be... dangerous. ...
And even in case you find those plans, there are a lot of other factors and requirements to count in as well: ...

Captain Caveworm a true hero and I know people who have seen him like my grandma.
Goodbye, still got some work to do. Check back later if you want.
Ahoyyy there, you might be just who I'm looking for. I need some help on an adventure ...
I do have something that's been bothering me as of late. On the closest island, Aragonia, some pirates crash landed.

Ever since they arrived, these pirates have been wreaking havoc on the surrounding islands and capturing wild turtles, including Targuna itself. Could you help me and this island by taking care of this threat with that?
I am Skjaar the Mage, master of all spells.
Once I was the master of all mages, but now I only protect this crypt.
To those who have lived for a thousand years time holds no more terror.
I'm not here to help anybody. I only protect my master's crypt.
This door seals a crypt.
Here lies my master. Only his closest followers may enter.
If you are one of his followers, you need not ask about him, for you will know. And if you aren't, you are not worthy anyway!
Hundreds of years my master's castle stood on the top of this mountain. Now there is a volcano.
The castle was destroyed when my master tried to summon a nameless creature. All that is left is this volcano.
I can still feel the magical energy in the volcano.
I will give the key to the crypt only to the closest followers of my master. Would you like me to test you?

My name is Aneus, the storyteller.
I'm a storyteller.
The story of Carlin is closely related to the story of the Fields of Glory. If you are interested in details, ask me about the story.
Thais is an ancient city. It has its origin in a hamlet called Tradespot. To learn more about its growth and rise, ask someone else. I don't know this story.
The elves love stories. I learnt a lot while I lived in their city for a while. You should travel there and talk to the elves, too, and don't forget to visit their library.
Most cities have small libraries filled with treasures in the form of stories. The biggest library is located in the White Raven Monastery.
The White Raven Monastery houses the biggest library in the known world. The monks there are a bit reclusive, though, and the Isle of the Kings is somewhat difficult to reach.
The Isle of the Kings is the burial place of the Thaian nobility. For many centuries each king and many nobles have been buried there.
I don't know much about him. I only know that he's selling fish in the village.
A lovely woman. Still, I give you a hint: Better stay away from her! <grins>
I don't know much about him. He sails much and he has seen nearly the whole world.
The dwarfs have a rich history and like to tell about it. Actually some dwarfs are so old that they experienced many events in history themselves.
The gods had great influence on humanity and other races. There are many stories related to them ...
In fact, there are so many stories that it won't be sufficient to talk to some people, you will also have to research many books to learn about them.
The stories about him are stories of grief, revenge and destruction. You can hear them almost everywhere. My story deals with similar topics but with other people.
This is a story for another day.
Well, if you wish, I can tell you the story about this place here - the story about the Fields of Glory!
Well, if you wish, I can tell you the story about this place here - the story about the Fields of Glory!
Ok, sit down and listen. Back in the early days, one of the ancestors of our king Tibianus III wanted to build the best city in whole Tibia.
Please forgive me. I forgot his name. I'm getting old.
The soldiers treated them like slaves.
You don't know what a slave is? I really hope that you will never have to make this experience.
It was the elite troop of the army. They were called the Red Legion (also known as the Bloody Legion).
The orcs attacked the workers from time to time and disturbed the work on the city.
All rebels were brought to the giant castle. Guarded by the Red Legion, they had to work and live in even worse conditions. ...
Also some friends of the king's sister were brought there.
The king's sister was pretty upset about the situation there but her brother didn't want to do anything about this matter. ...
So she made a plan to destroy the Red Legion for their cruelty forever.
The soldiers treated the workers like slaves.
She ordered her loyal druids and hunters to disguise themselves as orcs from the near island and to attack the Red Legion at night over and over again.
The General of the Red Legion became very angry about these attacks and after some months he struck back!
The General of the Red Legion became very angry about these attacks and after some months he struck back!
The soldiers of the Red Legion went to the island by night. The orcs were not prepared and the Red Legion killed hundreds of orcs with nearly no loss. ...
Afterwards, they walked back to the castle.
It is said that the orcish shamans cursed the Red Legion. ...
Nobody knows. But one third of the soldiers died due to a disease on the way back. ...
And the orcs wanted to take revenge, and after some days they struck back! ...
The orcs and many allied cyclopes and minotaurs from all over Tibia came to avenge their friends and killed nearly all workers and soldiers in the castle. ...
The help of the king's sister arrived too late.
She tried to rescue the workers but it was too late. The orcs started immediately to attack her troops, too. ...
Her royal troops went back to the city. A trick saved the city from destruction.
They used the same trick they had used against the Red Legion, and the orcs started to fight their non-orcish allies. ...
After a bloody and long fight, the orcs went back to their cities. The city of Carlin was rescued. ...
Ever since, a woman has been ruling over Carlin and this statue was made to remind us of their great tactics against the orcs and the Red Legion. ...
So that was the story of Carlin and the Fields of Glory. I hope you liked it. <smiles>

So you don't know it yet. This island, Grimvale, is affected by were-sickness. Many pitiful, who are stricken with the curse, dwell in the tunnels and caverns underneath the village and the nearby hurst.
Yes, pitiful. For they are savage beasts now who regularly come up from below to attack the village. But once they were inhabitants of Grimvale, before they changed.

Through a bite or even a scratch, you may be infected with the were-sickness. If that happens, there is little hope - until the next full moon you'll change into a were-creature, depending on the animal that hurt you.

There is a plant, the purple nightshade. It blossoms exclusively in the light of the full moon and only underground, where the full moon's light is falling through fissures in the surface. Only this plant's blossoms are able to defeat the were-sickness.
It transforms peaceful villagers into savage beasts. We're not sure how this curse found the way into our small village. But one day it began. At first it befell just a few people. ...
In a full moon night they changed into bears and wolves, and tore apart their unsuspecting relatives while they were asleep. ...
Those merely wounded, first thought they were lucky. But then we realised they were changing, too. Later, others assumed the forms of badgers and boars also. ...
But that does not mean they were any less wild or dangerous than the others.
We are not sure what they are doing down there. We're glad if they stay in the caverns and leave us alone. Only at full moon do they come up and threaten the island's surface and village. ...
I, however, have a hunch as to why they dwell so deep under the earth.
There are old legends about a subterranean temple that was once built in this area. Supposedly many artefacts are still hidden down there. ...
I don't have the time to tell you the entire tale, but there is a book here in which you may read the whole story.

If you bring me a common leghold trap and some liquid silver, I may be able to create a silvered trap for you. You could use it to weaken even a powerful were-creature.
He's basically a ferryman nowadays, but I remember when he was our village's leading fisherman. He offers a ferry service between Grimvale and Edron. You must have met him - he sailed you here.
He's an experienced hunter and knows much about the woods, the animals that dwell there, and about the werewolves. He's devoted himself to finding out everything there is to know about the Curse.

She's an old druid. She's been living here on Grimvale since she was a little girl, just like me. She's very interested in were-creature body parts. If you find any, I'm sure she will love to trade with you.
The small island you are standing on. For a long time it was a peaceful and placid place. But lately it has become more dangerous.
The simple huts you see scattered here. The village is called Grimvale, like the same-named island.

Yes, many centuries ago a big temple was built underneath the island of Grimvale. It was incidentally rediscovered a few years back when one of the village children got lost in the tunnels underneath the island, and found the temple ruins. ...
I wrote down all information about it in my notebook here. Feel free to read it, if you are interested in the temple.
Every month around the 13th, the single Tibian moon will by fully visible to us. That's when the curse hits us hardest. ...

The two days around the 13th, the 12th and the 14th, are considered 'Harvest Moon', those are the best to gather nightshade. However, only after it has reached its apex on the 13th, the curse strengthens. ...
We do not know what happens down there in those tunnels around that time but there is a presence there, we all feel - yet cannot quite fathom. ...
At full moon, humans transform into wild beasts: wolves, boars, bears and others. Some call it the Curse of the Full Moon, others think it is a kind of sickness. ...
During this time, we try to not leave the house, we shut the windows and hope it will pass. The curse will weaken a bit after that but it returns. Every month.
Farewell, then.
Oh, hello dear visitor. Be welcome to participate in the festivities.
Isn't it always surprising how fast time flies? The years have positively flown by in a mist of happiness.
Some of you have been witnesses to the evolution of this world, others have only recently begun their journey with us and still have so much to learn about the past.
From humble beginnings something special has been forged in the fire of the hardships of time to metamorphose into something that is so beautiful for so many.

In the beginning there was only an idea, a vision. Back then no one could foresee how things would evolve. The past has shown that the world can change the course of the people and the people can change the course of the world. ...
Fates have crossed and parted. None of these encounters were insignificant. Even small pebbles make large waves, especially so, when one life impacts upon another. ...
This little idea which was born so many, many years ago has influenced so many, many lives throughout the whole world. In return many hands have helped to shape and refine that idea.
It is in the nature of things to start out small and shaky just like a toddler taking its first steps. The world is continuously growing and changing. Hopefully for the better. ...

And just as it takes a village to raise a child, it takes a community to grow a world. The past laid the foundation for a plethora of ideas and concepts, which have combined in unique ways to become what we know today.
It has been a long journey but what a ride it has been! Imagination led to adventure. Friends were made and lost, people fell in love and got married. Everything because of this little idea. ...
A vision has changed the world - at least a little bit. For some of us more than for others.
We live in a world that is changing and growing. This is a wonderful thing. It has been such a fascinating time we have shared.
Time moves on and now the time has come again to celebrate and to look back and to remember.
Good times, come on! It's a celebration! Just look around and have fun! Talk about it. Tell people about your experiences and memories. Take some time to listen to their stories. ...
Don't be a wallflower! Join in! It is you who we are celebrating here.
In the end the whole world is nothing but a blank canvas, waiting to be filled with your experiences, your stories of friendship and hardship, of drama and love.
In the end your experiences are part of our story - the story of a journey, of growth, of maturity. We all have created this together. Without each other none of this would exist. ...

Thank you for listening! Thank you for forging friendships! Thank you for going on adventures! Thank you for exploring! Thank you for being a part of it! It is truly you who is truly celebrated here and now. Thank you! Thank you for everything!
It's a fine day to celebrate.

My duties hardly leave me time to visit the town. I don't like crowded streets and too many people anyway. I rather prefer a walk along the beach, to watch the sea from the cliffs or to listen to the music of wind and waves.

The town of Darashia is built around one of the few sweet water supplies of Darama. It is famous for its sand wasp honey and its sandworm stew.
The dreaded town of Drefia was once a haven for heretics, necromancers and demon worshippers. Its was destroyed in the war of the Djinn.
The desert lands of Darama are harsh and unforgiving. Therefore Daraman led his people there to found a new community based upon his teachings.

Daraman was a sage with ambition, that's for sure. His philosophy centred around the idea that by controlling yourself you could improve yourself. The closer you are coming to perfection, the closer you are to ascending to divinity.

Malor was second in power only to Gabel and his followers among the Djinn were many. It was not easy for the evil Djinn to change their ways, and many preferred to follow Malor instead of Gabel. In the end a civil war erupted.

In the war of the Djinn citys were levelled, lands were cursed and islands sunk. Finally, Malor was caught and imprisoned in an enchanted bottle. His followers fled this plane, while the good djinn laid to rest to recover their strength.
Gabel was the most powerful among the Djinn lords. He was cruel and merciless, until one day his minions brought a certain human to him whom they had captured and tortured.
This human showed no fear and did not yield under torture. They could bend him, but they never managed to break him. Impressed by this mortal, Gabel talked to him and learned about his philosophy.
The human whom the Djinn had caught was none other but Daraman. The mighty Gabel was intrigued by his philosophy and changed his ways according to Daraman's teachings.

The teachings of asceticism, inner peace and ascension appealed to the Djinn, although in the beginning this was probably only because of his vanity and his greed for divinity. However, Malor and his followers opposed him.

This chalice was a tool of the gods which they created to make their task to create life easier. Zathroth who lacked the knowledge of creation stole that chalice and used it to spawn his evil minions.

The Djinn were the result of his first attempts. They were powerful and quite evil, but not as evil as Zathroth wished and quite independent in their thinking. Finally he discarded them and decided his second try would become his masterpiece.

Zathroth channelled all the hatred and foulness he could muster. He added the burning rage of his son Blog and mixed it with fire. The energy that was released destroyed the chalice, but Zathroth had succeeded in creating the first demon.

The archdemons are few, and extremely rare. And a good thing, too, for they are the rulers of the demon race. They are vain and powerhungry creatures who tend to form only small cabals and fight each other instead of allying against creation.
There are at least five demonic cabals of archdemons. The ruthless seven are the most prominent and powerful.
They are more than a myth, they are a horrible reality. It is possible that they still reside in the pits of inferno.
An infernal place in which the nightmare knights created a base to fight the minions of evil. It was lost when the Ruthless Seven conquered it.
The Nightmare Knights were an ancient order dedicated to fight evil. They were guided by prophetic dreams. The order ceased to exist after their war against the Brotherhood of Bones.
This brotherhood was an secret society of necromancers and followers of purest evil. They were vanquished long ago by their arch enemies, the Nightmare Knights.

The Triangle of Terror is a cabal of three archdemons that have put aside their quarrels to establish some power in the shadows of the Ruthless Seven. Although they are all very mighty demons, compared to one of the seven, they appear weak ...

So they try not to interfere much with the doings of the seven and look for power elsewhere. Their members are Morgaroth, the schemer, Ghazbaran, the lord of blades and Zoralurk, the demon with the thousand faces.

Morgaroth belongs to the cabal Triangle of Terror. He usually has minions to do his work rather than doing it himself. Although sometimes he enters our world in person to inspire the fear his cabal is built upon.
Ghazbaran is a member of the demonic cabal Triangle of Terror. He likes the physical challenge and combat as much as the pain and death he inflicts.
Zoralurk is said to be a member of the demon cabal called Triangle of Terror. She is rumoured to wander the lands in many disguises, poisoning the body and minds of people by word or deed.

Orshabaal is one of the many servants of the Ruthless Seven. By far weaker than his masters, he seems to have developed some kind of inferiority complex which he tries to compensate by raiding our world and slaying as many innocents as he can.

The ancient structures that were found deep beneath the ghostlands were built by an unkown race for an unknown purpose. It's quite certain that, whatever they were once used for, they now cause madness and ghost sightings in the surrounding area.
Whatever the original meaning of that underground complex was, it is now like an open wound in the nearby lands, spreading madness and attracting all kinds of ghosts and apparitions.
I think you are referring to the beast Hugo that is said to still haunt the Plains of Havoc. The legends which tell of this creature are ancient and almost forgotten.

As far as we know, once a terrible beast roamed the lands we now call the Plains of Havoc. It was so fierce that no one dared to even dream about killing it. It was finally tricked by the knight Endulos.
Endulos was not a great warrior, but a man of wit and genius. After many of his brethren of the Nightmare Knights had fallen prey to the beast, he came up with a cunning plan to end this threat.
He lured Hugo into a trap. Bound by roots and stones charged with powerful magic he could not move anymore. Now, the beast lies trapped in a hidden cave for all eternity.
The legends tell us that the Nightmare Knights trapped it beneath one of their fortresses, or rather that they built a fortress on top of his eternal prison.
Somewhere in the Plains of Havoc, where the Necromant King was defeated, lies the secret entrance to the Pits of Inferno.
The Necromant King. He is dead forever, and that is the nicest thing I can say about him. May he rot in his tomb.
If Tibia is a fallen god, does that makes us the maggots crawling on it?
A city in the far north. It separated itself from the Thaian kingdom about 100 years ago. Now it is ruled by a dynasty of queens.
Edron is the latest colony of the Thaian kingdom. However, structures of an earlier colonisation have been found. We cannot tell if those inhabitants were human or of any other known race.
Thais is the capital of an ancient human kingdom. Once its rule was more or less undisputed. In the years the strength of the Thaian kingdom eroded by different events.
The underground city of the minotaurs can be reached through a dangerous passage from the old temple.
Behind the mountain lies a land of great danger.
The ancient fortress city of the dwarfs was carved into the mountain known as 'The Big Old One'. It is quite hidden and heavily guarded to withstand any assault.

The small but strong dwarves are tireless workers and fierce warriors. They are familiar with several crafts and mastered most of them. In our days their smithing skills are rivalled only by those of the cyclopses.

The gods created the vortex to guide powerful souls to our world so they might join the battle for creation.
Venore is a centre of commerce and trade. Its ambitious trade barons are nominally subjects of the Thaian kingdom.
The swamp city is a centre of commerce, and known for it riches and its merchant barons. It is part of the Thaian kingdom.
Although lovely, the city of the elves lacks the grace and the vibrance of the elven cities of old. The elves are still working on improvement of their settlement.
The elves of Shadowthorn are hosile to intruders. Their Kuridai leaders practise some sinister cults and the other castes are more their minions then their equals.
The elven society is dividded into certain castes, the cenath, the kuridai, the deraisim, the abdaisim and the legendary teshial.
The Abdaisim are what humans would call 'independent elves'. They take shelter wherever they might find it, are wanderers and explorers. They only keep loose contact with the elven society.
The Cenath favour magic above all other. They are the keepers of elven lore and wisdom. They are responsible for the astounding feats of druidic magic the elves are capable of.
One could call the Deraisim the scouts and rangers of elvenkind. Although all elves are formidable in that area, the Deraisim excel them all.

The Kuridai are the craftsmen and warriors of elvenkind. They are always moving, always scheming. They are the most aggressive elves and distrust outsiders. An outsider might be each non-Kuridai to them.
Its said that those elves were the masters of the dreams. Which many consider a special brand of magic. They seem to have vanished from the face of Tibia ages ago, however, and their fate is unknown.
Learn about the gods to learn from the gods.

Zathroth is the dark twin of Uman. They are one and they are two separate entities. We mortals can't really grasp this concept. He is the patron of dark magic and even darker secrets, the lust for dominance through cunning, and manipulation.

Uman is the light twin of Zathroth. Their unity and separation at once is a concept we cannot hope to grasp. He is the patron of light magic, the knowledge that benefits all and brings progress to the society.
Blog is the god of rage and fierce battle. He's also the patron of power, although a power to oppress and bully others around. He is the son of Zathroth and one of the Tibian suns.

Cyclopses are seen as the smiths of Blog, whom they call 'the ragehammer' or 'ragehammerer'. Indeed their skills create mostly crude and nasty-looking weapons and armor, but which are incredibly effective nonetheless.
A shame he's gone. He could have become somewhat of a tourist magnet.

This ring will give you limited protection against any kind of damage.
These rings improve your regenerative powers, accelerating the recovery of both your mana and your lifeforce.
These rings were created by an ancient, long since forgotten race. It is said they valued secrecy above all. They used these magic rings to make themselves invisible.
This ring will increase your skill when wielding swords.
This ring increases the rate with which you heal your physical wounds.

Sadly, the secret where to mine or how to create this ore has been lost in the course of time.
This is the metal of 'evil', the hell-forged iron no ordinary flames can melt. It is rumoured to be harvested in hell from iron rocks in which damned souls were imprisoned.
This steel absorbs magic. While it is of inferior quality compared to ordinary steel, its absorbing qualities make it important though.
What makes this black steel exceptional is its lightness and peculiar property of lacking the common steel 'noise'. It is also called 'silent steel' or 'thief's steel' for this reason.
The luminescent brightsteel is used for artwork mainly. In ancient times, items of great magic power were crafted using brightsteel. Those crafts were lost with the races who held the secret to them.
The dwarfs call it heartiron and claim it is part of the heart of The Big Old One. Therefore, they hold it sacred and its use is limited and regulated.
The dwarven high steel is relatively common but expensive and still hard to come by. The elite dwarven weaponry and armours are made of Uth'Doon.
The so-called dreamsilver is a legendary metal. Almost everything we know about it are rumours only.
The ancient dwarven kings forged it using magic metal , which they took from cyclopses who found it in the heart of a fallen star.

And after all those years, surviving several generations, this female shaman is still their leader.
It's an old tale but it persists in the minds of the Svargrondar. It is about my father. There are rumours that he is still alive. ...

People regularly report about seeing him on top of the cliff right next to Svargrond. I myself would be glad if finally his corpse were found. Then I would be jarl 'Sven the Elder' ..... sounds much better.
We heard that this mythical dwarf lives somewhere on the southern Ice Islands.
I don't sell anything. If the people accept you, they might be willing to trade with you.

We understand that our friends from Carlin are wary with the realm ruled by Thais but this is not of our concern.
It's some light side of mythical powers. Such things should only be dealt with by druids or shamans.
We did not allow them to stay here. This had nothing to do with our friendship with Carlin but for the way they handled things and their harmful approach to go hunting.
For more than two generations no ship had reached our shores because the giant sea serpents attacked and sank most ships that tried to travel here. ...
Not long ago the sea serpents disappeared as suddenly as they had come. Now ships visit us again on a regular base.

The yetis are mythical beasts. Only few that encountered those creatures lived to tell the tale. The chakoyas worship them as divine beings, although they have no real relations to them as far as we can tell.
May wind and weather be with you, Player.

Well, we honour Father Earth and Mother Fire. Some of us even follow the teachings of additional gods.
Well, I'm the emperor of the dwarfs. It's my duty to protect my folk and to see that justice is done.
Well, go and see the wonders of our cities for yourself.

Well, more than 150 years ago, my father lost his beard overnight. Thereupon, he resigned from his leadership after hundreds of years of supreme ruling.

Well, we use all stocked resources of finest metal to craft weapons and armor, we train new warriors and spellcasters every day. ...
We give battle training to each citizen to enable them to better defend themselves and to form militia units in case of emergency. And we call in old favours and allies.
Well, all dwarfs could be considered citizens. We are brothers and sisters in fire and earth.
Well, after some centuries I stopped to worry about time.
Well, you claim there is another dwarven city called Beregar? Could that be the city of the ancient tribe?!?
Well, our race is very hot-blooded, bullheaded, and also proud. The real cause is unknown but I can imagine how it happened.

Well, it must have been written by someone of the Kazordoon tribe as there hasn't been any contact to the other tribe since the day we parted. I doubt you'll find a written copy of it here as it has been passed on by word of mouth. ...
Maybe you find someone who tells you the poem. I for myself don't have time to tell you a children's poem. By the beard of my father, I'm the emperor, jawoll!
WAAAH! Don't mention that beast! He was after the bones of our ancestors last time King Tibianus visited us!
Well, the gods handed the lands over to the younger races, but my people will leave this world in dignity.
Well, the gods handed the lands over to the younger races, but my people will leave this world in dignity.

Well, well, well, the god blade. A myth? Perhaps. Even in my youth, it was only a legend.
Well, I'm fine, the last centuries have been good to me, jawoll.

Well, our mines have been invaded by a basilisk. We trapped him with a cave-in. The hero who brings me the body of this beast will get a great reward. ...
But of course after the blight we have other problems down there, like the lost and the renegades.
Well, the blight was a great disaster. It hit us completely unprepared. ...

Given the severity of the disaster, we can be glad we handled it that well. Still, it weakened our defences, and by chance or sinister plans our enemies took it as an opportunity to hit us even harder. ...
In the midst of recovering from the blight and relocating resources, the trouble in the mines began. First with rampaging creatures and then came the Lost. ...
With resources bound there, even here in Kazordoon an enemy rose his ugly head ... and this head wore a dwarfen beard. Our own people, lead by the Axe of Vengeance fellowship.
Well, the Axes of Vengeance were troublemakers even when they were few. Their reckless ways and boasting sadly impressed a lot of the young and easily gullible. ...
Stories of their mostly made-up exploits and lies lured some into their embrace, but it was not until the blight that they became popular and a threat thanks to their leader, Jarok Bilespit.

Well, Jarok Bilespit was a mercenary. He did many questionable things for money. Especially dealing with non-dwarfs, although he usually was the first to express their disgust for them, when not taking their money, of course. ...

He gathered around him a number of drunkards and bullies of the worst sort, and founded the Axes of Vengeance fellowship, which was rather his private gang than a true fellowship. ... Emperor Kruzak: They were usually travelling on contract, doing questionable missions and only returned to Kazordoon to boast about their made-up exploits and to spend their ill-begotten money with both hands. ...
This impressed certain people and gained him an undeserved reputation as a daring hero. ...

Though no week they were in town passed without one of them getting imprisoned for brawls, threats and destruction of property, especially younger dwarfs thought it would be cool to be one of them, and if not respected, then at least be feared. ...

When the blight struck, his easy explanations and pointless accusations stroke a cord in the minds of several individuals. I admit we did not see this coming and let him spread his phrases in the city. ...
We had other things to do and did not want more unrest by arresting some popular figure. With our attention elsewhere, Bilespit took advantage of the desperate and lured them into his ranks. ...
He was never the subtle type though, so it became quite clear what unspeakable treason he planed. ...

When he led his bunch of mercenaries and several drunks as some kind of meat-shield to dethrone me, we were prepared. We planned to take Bilespit down first to minimize casualties, but things got out of hand and there were many deaths on both sides. ...

With the order to keep presumably innocent casualties low, my guards fought very restricted, which could have led to their losing the battle. So we had to change orders to reduce our own casualties, and the fight turned very bloody and nasty. ...
Rumours spread through the city and others who thought they sympathized with Bilespit's cause joined the battles. ...
Still, we tried to keep casualties low; and as soon as we took certain strategic positions and gained the upper hand, most of the rebellious forces escaped. ...
Now they are hiding in the mine: Most of those mines are old and depleted of ore. They are overrun by all sorts of creatures such as the Lost. ...

So it made not much sense to send in troops that could not efficiently use their numbers and combat training in brawls within winding and narrow tunnels. We had to sent in troops to fight the advancing lost, though.

Oh, Thais, I'll be back. One day, I'll be back.
My good old cousin Sam. Oh, how I miss him.
Oh, what an endearing little girl, and she's working so hard to help me, even without receiving payment. Such a sweet little girl!

He's just like his cousin Willie.
An old woman shouldn't be treated like that, no way, that's bad.

I knew it! I knew she would try to get the monopoly on potions in this village! But no one has listened to me!
What a hero, what a hero.
I don't know how anyone could give up the flourishing business she led. She should have listened to me and find someone who continues that business for her.

I wish I could help you with that, but no, I was told to stick to weapons. Go see Lily.
Well, the mainland also consists of several continents. You can go there once you are level 8 and have talked to the oracle.
The oracle, ah, such a weird being! It will lead you off this island once you are level 8, yes it will, mark my words.
I think good practice is better than reading a boring book. Of course, you will need proper equipment to be able to get practice!
As an adventurer you should always have at least a backpack, a rope, a shovel, a weapon, an armor and a shield.
Good monsters to start with are rats. They live in the sewers under the village of Rookgaard.
There are many sewer entrances throughout Rookgaard. One is right outside this shop and to the left. For more details about monsters and dungeons, best talk to one of the guards.
The king encouraged salesmen to travel here, but only I dared to take the risk, and a risk it was!
The bridge guard Dallheim is north of here, just follow the street, you can't miss it.
It's really heart-warming to see how the Tibia economy is prospering.
Oh, you're welcome, very welcome.
Greetings!
My name is Larek. Some call me Larek the Wayfarer, because of my voyages to many faraway lands.

I like to think of myself as a discoverer and explorer of unknown regions and cultures. At the moment I'm acting as a kind of merchant. It is a convenient way to get Vuzrog's permission to live here for a time without getting eaten.
Unfortunately I lost my watch some weeks ago when exploring the steppe and cataloguing the plant life.
As I heard the shaman, Ghorza, is worried these days. She thinks the Great Hunger is upset.

Ogres worhip the Great Hunger, a kind of spirit being they believe will eat up the entire world if not fed regularly. Therefore they often perform rites of sacrifice - with food but also with living creatures, to feed this entity.

The Explorer Society is an elite society of adventurers that explore and research all aspects of our world. We are interested in the many different creatures of Tibia, as well as the history of curious structures and items.

The ogres are simple, warlike people, more interested in a fight and good food than in politics. Ogres like conflict; they are impulsive and quick to anger. They prefer to solve conflicts through combat rather than words. ...

They are distrustful towards strangers like us and tend to welcome them with avoidance in the best case. Lately yet, the Bloody Skulls tribe here has shown a sort of interest in trade with other peoples.

An honorable death is not the highest purpose in an ogre's life, but rather a fulfilled life, which primarily means enough food and a comfortable hut. Food carries great weight in ogre life and society.

The ogres are a tribal people, divided into several different clans. Leader of a tribe is usually the strongest male ogre. The chieftain is supported by an ogre-shaman. If the shaman is female, the two are often, but not necessarily, a couple.
The strongest male ogre is a tribe's chieftain. For the Bloody Skulls this is Vuzrog, at least at the moment. But Ghorza seems to expect that a younger ogre will challenge him soon.
He's the chieftain of the Bloody Skulls tribe and, to be honest, he is the exemplary ogre: big, strong, always hungry, blunt and not very clever. ...
But as he is the strongest individual of this tribe, he also is the big boss, as the ogres often call the chieftain.

Ghorza is the tribe's shaman. I have the impression that she is a rather unusual ogress, because she's interested in humans not only in the sense of a tasty snack. She seems to think that we could be useful to her and the tribe.

The shaman is very important for an ogre tribe. Often, but not always, the shaman is an elder ogress. She cares for the spiritual welfare of the tribe, appeases the spirits, blesses newborn ogre-children and the like. ...
This tribe's shaman is Ghorza.
He's one of the ogres living here. He studied me for a while and now seems to imitate my behavior. He dabbles in trading now, buying different things. ...
You could talk to him but I suppose, he'll not make a trade with you without the chieftain's permission.
He's strong but narrow-minded even by ogre standards. He's not often here in the village so I have seen him just a few times. And it's better that way for I assume he's cruel and sadistic.
He's a goblin who is being kept as a slave by the chieftain Vuzrog. Poor little fellow.

There are quite a few goblins living here in Krailos. I suppose they originally arrived as stowaways on the ships that now and then burst at Krailos' rocky shores. Most of these goblins are kept as slaves by the ogres. ...
As are other smaller races like dworcs or coryms.
That's the tribe living in this village. They are one of the settled clans, whilst others are still nomadic. In addition, they seem to be the only tribe so far that tolerates humans. ...
Mainly because the shaman sees a benefit in our presence.

Ogres value food above all things. They like meat or beer, but as I found out they also adore sweets! They're downright scoffing them. But they don't know how to make cookies or candy. And at this point the humans come in. ...
As far as I'm concerned, I survive amongst the ogres because I play the role of a merchant here. I provide them with sweets, they let me live here and pursue my studies about Krailos.

Krailos is this vast grassland and steppe you are standing in, and is mainly populated by ogres. The region is located north of Oramond, bordered by high mountains to the south and a wild sea to the east, west and north. ...
It's a secluded area, but it seems to has a very interesting history.
Oramond lies south of here, separated from Krailos by a high mountain chain. It's very different from the ogre lands, but also dangerous. Many minotaurs live there.
Krailos is surrounded by many underwater shelves. They make it difficult for ships to reach the coast unscathed. At the rugged shores you may find the one or other shipwreck.
Once a sophisticated, but peaceful grassland empire existed on this peninsula. It was noted for its advanced architecture and philosophy. ...
But it was destroyed hundreds of years ago through social breakdown, caused by their interest in forbidden things. ...

In this empire the ogres were not quite slaves, but rather a kind of deprived lower class. Yet it seems they were the only ones to survive the downfall of this ancient realm, perhaps simply because of their physical strength.

The humans who lived here so long ago worshipped the suns of our world. Not only the calm and considerate Suon but also his reckless and wild sister Fafnar. As far as I found out, the veneration of these two aspects was in balance for a long time. ...
But the adherents to the wild goddess Fafnar prevailed and the destructive nature of their goddess eventually caused the downfall of this ancient empire.

Suon is one of the two suns of our world, considered as one of the gods, the son of Fardos, by many. Some call him the Life-Bringing Sun and believe that he observes creation with love and blesses us with warmth and growth. ...
Others guess he is just the misguided sibling of Fafnar and that his light turns pale compared to her brightness.

Fafnar is one of the two suns of our world, considered as one of the gods, the daughter of Fardos, by many. Some call her the Scorching Sun and believe that she observes creation with hate and jealousy. ...
But others think she's the stronger of the two suns, that Suon's light turns pale compared to her brightness.
Fardos is considered the creator, often called the Great Observer. Many people believe that it was his doing that we possess divine souls.
Yes, the drying of seas and rivers is a big problem in Krailos. Gradually, all sources of fresh water are fading away. If you want to know more, you should ask Ghorza.
The ogres love them. If you need cookies I could sell you some. Of course, you also might try to bake them yourself. In that case I could sell you flour and milk.
Unfortunately, I don't have one at the moment. But you could try to bake one yourself. I could sell you flour and milk. If you find some fruit to decorate it, you could bake a tasty cake.
No, I don't sell beer. The ogres brew beer themselves, they have no need of a merchant selling it.
The ogres regularly eat prickly pears which grow on the big cactus trees everywhere in the steppe. Often ogres carry some with them as a kind of provisions. ...
That a tasty juice can be made of these fruit was a new experience for the ogres. If you'd like to press out some juice, I can sell you a squeezer.

Ogres mainly eat the meat of the clomp, a large pachyderm which resembles a crossing between a mammoth and a rhino. The ogres also eat the raw meat, but they prefer it roasted. Of course, they're also eating ... uhm, men now and then.
The clomp, as the ogres call this animal, is a large pachyderm which resembles a crossing between a mammoth and a rhino. Clomps are the largest animals in Krailos. ...
But although they are very strong and have a reputation for being tough, they are quite easily hunted by the ogres, as the clomps visit water holes daily and can be killed while they drink.

The shaman Ghorza has a hyaena, her totem animal. I heard that it ran away some days ago. Unfortunately I have no idea where the beast could be. Hm ... But I guess the goblin Nibble might know something. He mentioned a hyaena in a small cave.
You can find these quartzes all over the steppe. They have an orange tone with a golden shade and are often half-buried in the steppe sand.

I have, indeed, a small depot here. I found the buried ruins of some small rooms right under my tent and used them to establish a depot and a bank. But before I open the grille for you I'd ask you a small favour.

Science can be a hard way to earn your living, you know. So I thought it would be wise to find another subsistence, just in case. The bank is in a subterranean room under my tent. But before I open the grille for you I'd ask you a small favour.
But that would be such an important contribution to science in general and botany in particular! Please think it over again. Perhaps you'll change your mind.

If I don't provide the ogres with enough sweets like cookies and candy, the chieftain, Vuzrog, no longer will see my benefit for this village and eat me up. So I can't leave the village for too long. ...

I am the gatekeeper of Ashta'daramai. That's what Gabel told me to do. You know - keeping the courtyard clean, getting rid of salesmen, keeping Efreet vermin out... that kind of thing. But in my spare time I work as a part-time philosopher.

Yes. Comes with the job. You see - here I am, sitting on the same chair all day and staring at the same blank wall. So what happens is that my mind starts wandering. And, you know, I start thinking. You know - about all kinds of things.
Yes. About the world and the gods and all that. And about girls. Yes, about girls, mostly.
You did not know there are female djinns, did you? That's because they are quite rare. They are the greatest treasures of our race, and we guard them jealously.

This place is the Marid's safe haven. No enemy has ever managed to take this fortress by assault, and we will see to it that it stays this way.
That is the Efreet's fortress. I have never seen it, but I'm sure it can't compare to this place.
When I look up from my wall, what do I see? Huge, forbidding mountains! No wonder I feel claustrophobic.
Ah yes - the desert. I still remember how beautiful that land was back in the days before the war. ...
A land full of song and bliss it was - a veritable paradise. Fa'hradin once said its destruction was a supreme example of the transitoriness of all things mortal. ...
I am not sure I agree because I don't know what 'transitoriness' means.
Tibia is a beautiful world. Not that I see much of it, staring at this wall night and day.
They say Darashia is a beautiful human city somewhere to the north. I would really love to see it, but I can't abandon my post.

I understand the humans have founded some beautiful cities. I would like to see them, but as long as I have to stay here that won't happen. Which means I will not go anywhere as long as the war goes on.

I guess you know about the background and there is no need to tell you that the forces from beyond managed to acquire the parts of the godbreaker in a coup.
The godbreaker was created in ancient times, when the war between the gods and their minions was on its height. Its creation took aeons and incredible sacrifices. ...
Each part had to be crafted perfectly, to emulate the gods, so it would share 'the same place' with them. ...
Mere mortals can not even perceive it in his whole but only recognize the part of it that is the physical representation in our world. ...

If it was meant to be used as an actual weapon, as the ultimate threat, or if Zathroth was just tempted to use his knowledge in the ultimate way - to create something that could undo himself - we don't know. ...
However in the end even Zathroth deemed it too much of a threat but instead of destroying the contraption once and for all, it was disassembled and hidden away.
The secret locations of the godbreaker parts were revealed and due to trickery, the minions of Variphor acquired all of them.
The parts alone do them no good. To assemble the parts, great skill, immense power and forbidden knowledge are necessary. ...
The skill will be supplied by the fallen Yalahari and the power by Variphor itself. ...
The only thing they are still lacking is the knowledge to assemble and operate the godbreaker.
The godbreaker is a complex artifact. Incantation woven into incantation. The powers bound into it are so immense that the slightest mishandling could prove disastrous. ...
To figure out how it works, let alone how it can be operated safely, could require several centuries of tireless study. And even then this information would be only partial. ...
Yet the creation and operation of the godbreaker is just the kind of forbidden knowledge Zathroth values most, so it was compiled and stored.
Of course the dangers of such knowledge were obvious. It was hidden in a sacred place devoted to Zathroth and dangerous knowledge. ...
The hidden library, the forbidden hoard, the shrouded trove of knowledge or the veiled hoard of forbidden knowledge, the place has many names in many myths.
The myths agree that the place is well hidden, extremely guarded and contains some of the most powerful pieces of knowledge in this world and probably beyond. ...
However the knowledge about the godbreaker now poses a threat to all existence. In the hands of Variphor it can cause disaster in previously unknown ways. The gods themselves are in peril.
Regardless of the dangers, the cult of Zathroth refused to destroy the knowledge of the godbreaker for good. ...
They value dangerous knowledge that much, that they are unable to part from it, even when faced with the utter destruction of creation.
This leaves us with no choice but to take action into our own hands.
You have to find the veiled hoard of Zathroth, breach it and destroy the knowledge how to use the godbreaker.
I know it's asked much but it's no longer a matter of choice. ...
The enemy is moving and I have reports that suggest the minions of Variphor are actively searching for Zathroth's library. They must not be allowed to succeed. ...
We must be the first to reach the hoard and make sure the enemy doesn't get the information he needs.
I'd recommend to follow the few leads me and my associates could gather so far. ...
Old myths, some rumours about old texts and other pieces of knowledge that I could use to figure out where to locate the hidden library and how to enter it.
My associates prefer to remain unnamed and I understand and respect that.
Hints about the shrouded hoard are numerous, though most are general mentions in texts that deal with Zathroth. But there are other sources. ...

My leads are the museum in Thais, something strange in the Darashian desert, rumours about fishmen, an ancient order, the mysterious asuri, or a lost isle?
I'm a follower of Uman, the god of knowledge and wisdom. I'm part of a circle of people who are aware of the threat to our world caused by the entity Variphor. ...
We try our best to shield ourselves while watching the steps of the enemy of all things. Even we do not fully grasp it's non-existence. Nor should we try to do so.
We don't ask Uman for guidance but for wisdom. It is up to ourselves to find solutions and to use our knowledge appropriately.
The concept of Variphor is extremely hard to comprehend. It's the contradiction that gives birth to a mockery of purpose. It is the antithesis to existence. ...
More than nonexistence. Or less, so to say. However, that thing has no sentience in a way we know. It has no plans, no purpose yet it somehow moves and feeds upon our world. ...
His puppets, the tainted like the Yalahari, are a mere conduit. Their collective existence gives the un-thing a mockery of perception in a mind-wracking way. ...
Other than that, the thing from beyond just reacts to our plane of existence. Although it knows no rules and is not bound by any, in contact with our plane this somehow changed in a twisted way. ...
That what has no purpose, now has a purpose at the same time. This dichotomy rips logic apart and is what actually makes it happen. Contradiction creates its anchor.
Right now the un-thing is occupied with worming its way into our world and its grasp is already tight. So its name alone has lost some of its taint right now. ...
It's still advised to use the name sparsely as things might change fast.
In the past, giving it a name made it more tangible, dragged it a little more into our world and even worse, into the mind of those who used that name or definition. ...
By thinking about it, 'it', which knew no existence at all, became a bit more existent in the minds of those who knew about it. This concentration poisoned the minds it occupied. ...
It's not that something actually enslaved them, but they changed, became less a part of existence and more like that un-thing, more part of it. ...
Even worse, being contradictions themselves, they became the fuel this thing needed to breach our world. ...

We guess the vanishing of the Yalahari, who came to know of the un-thing out there only to reappear in the present centuries later, hints they were absorbed or annihilated by Variphor and what we now see are projections or recreations of some sorts. ...
Something that was devoured and reborn as part of Variphor in some way.

Human society has been polluted by the taint of magic like many of Tibia's civilisations.

Sadly, even my own people distrust us and our technology to some extent. They think we are 'different' and some of the ancients condemn us because we don't align ourselves with the elemental forces. ...
It's not that we don't honour the elements, we do. But we have a different approach to honouring the elements. ...
This difference is the source of the distrust, but despite this, our inventions have become an integral part of dwarven society and we are acknowledged for our accomplishments.
Magic is unreliable, restrictive and hampers progress. ...
I know, you're thinking 'he's just jealous and wants technomancy to get more attention' but it's not only technology that is held back by the quick fixes magic provides - society suffers as well. ...
Consider this. There is a spell for everything so nobody tries to find alternative solutions for their problems - the need for creative thinking disappears and people become lazy. ...

People become trapped by their superstions because they know someone only needs to mutter a few words to turn them into a frog and suddenly, the whole world is full of people putting the evil eye on you. ...
They blame fate for their problems rather than taking responsibility for their own lives. . ...
Of course, some of these arguments could be used against technology, but at least there is skill and thought behind technology, not just some hocus pocus gobbledygook!
Regardless of what those narrowminded spellcasters claim, technomancy is a science in its own right. It is much more precise than dabbling in magic and incomprehensible forces. ...
And, what's more, it's based on logical thinking - not some freaky talent you have to be born with. ...
Of course I understand why you humans prefer to rely on chance and childrens' rhymes without having any true understanding of what you are doing. ...
As a technomancer, you can at least work out your mistakes because they are based on logic, even if the mistake you have made is likely to have blown someone up . ...
That does not make our interaction with dwarven society an easy one, but we get along well enough.
Dwarfs are a race apart - a unique race. ...

I can fully understand the fact that other races such as humans and ... um ... elves and orcs and ... um ... cyclopes and ... hm ... flies and so on are in awe of us. But for us, our genius is an everyday fact of life. ...
Nevermind, human. Your inferiority is not your fault. Not every race can be as gifted as we are. Not that I mean to be rude or anything.

Hah! Elves! So blinded by their attachment to magic. If you were to ask them how a bow and arrow worked, they would probably tell you the spirits of the air carry their arrows to the hearts of their enemies! ...
They don't have the slightest idea of mechanics or physics.

Yes, yes. Fascinating issue. Hmm. Let's see .. I don't know too much about golems themselves, but I have a good idea about the mechanics involved. After researching some material that Telas sent me I was able to work out some crucial information. ...
Using the information I have put together, Telas should be able to pass on the specs to the blacksmiths. At least he can get the mechanical components organised.
Ah, yes, Telas. Quite smart for someone that tall.
Oh please. If you don't know what mechanics are about, go and find another dwarf who has a century to spare to explain it all to you. ...
I have more important things to do than show a human what a spanner is for.
From what has reached my ears it's quite a sight. I am not a big traveller so I don't really have an opinion and wouldn't be able to tell the difference between the truth and exaggeration. ...
But the word is that these Yalahari don't care much about keeping their machines in a good shape. What are they thinking of? Don't they know that a machine must be tended and cared for? ...
There is something odd going on in that city, I tell you. No-one who builds such wonders grows that careless.

Strange people, but that's no surprise considering they are not dwarfs. They had a good hand for technology though. Unfortunately they mixed it with magic which to my mind is as bad as watering beer, a crime! ...
Still, there is certainly a lot to be learned from their inventions. But they keep their secrets well guarded. I can understand and appreciate that.

What kind of a silly question is that? But fine: a machine is something that can do everything you can but twice as efficiently. And no, despite these qualities it doesn't have a tail, fur and above all, it doesn't eat bananas!
My greatest invention was the improved lift system that we used on the farms. It was by far more efficient and fast than the old ones. And what did those technophobic dwarfs go and do? ...
They made me a lift boy out of gratitude! They insisted that I had to operate it to guarantee its safety. What a joy I tell you! 'Lift me up Scutty' the whole stupid day! ...
Great! It took years for them to get used to the lift and let me move on to my other projects.
As you can see, I'm the tooth fairy. I collect children's teeth and wear a tutu and fly. ...

Ask a stupid question, get a stupid answer! What do you think all these machines are for? Why are my hands black with machine oil and why am I wearing a tool belt? No, I am not an unhygienic tooth fairy. ...
I am a technomancer! Master of machines and mechanics!

Being a paladin means to be always on the run. Not like running cowardly, of course, but we paladins like to keep our distance. Because - distance fighting is what we're best at! ...
We can handle all sorts of bows and throwing weapons instinctively well. Paladins can even use some magic, including the class-exclusive holy spells! Undead creatures will fear you, nyahahaha! ...

We also aren't as wimpy as those mages but have enough health to take a hit or two. Actually we can be quite good blockers with a shield. But as I said, it's all about being on the move! Run run run like the wind! Yay! ...
Uhm, what else to tell you... well, one thing you might need patience for is training. You will not hit anything well unless you invest some time in improving your distance skills. ...

Bleh, that can be boring! And well, you have to buy ammunition and carry all that stuff around with you. But that's really the only thing which I can think of that's not pure fun! You'll like being a paladin! ...
You can even get a vocation promotion and become a royal paladin once you've reached level 20! Doesn't that simply sound... royal? Teehee! If you need other information, let me know.
I like strong guys. Particularly those who carry my ammunition for me! Ask Hykrion if you're interested in that vocation.
They always take everything soooo serious and burn your butt with their fireballs! Ask Estrella if you're interested in that vocation.
Aww, druids are sweet. I know some really nice druids who always give me free heals. Ask Yandur if you're interested in that vocation.
All that talk about honour and stuff can be a bit cheesy, but I like the feeling of being protected!
She seems kinda arrogant, but she has a good heart. Really!
He's the kind of guy that always has a warm place for you. He's like a big brother to me!
I love the world of Tibia, especially the buzz in the cities!
Well I'm personally a fan of Carlin, but that's just me. The captain can give you more information about the Tibian cities.
Hooray for Carlin! A city ruled by girls! Tell me, what could go wrong??
He's always nice to me. He even calls me his 'little lady'. I like him, even though he's old!
He's always nice to me. He even calls me his 'little lady'. I like him, even though he's old!
I don't like the way he looks at me. It's so... greedy. And he seems to be happy when my spears break! Hmpf!
Oh yes, that's the best part! As a level 20 paladin, you can buy a vocation promotion and become a royal paladin. ...

Go to a royalty such as Queen Eloise in Carlin or King Tibianus in Thais and donate 20.000 gold pieces to become promoted. Not only will you have a fancy new title, but also better regeneration and other advantages!
Oh yes, that's the best part! As a level 20 paladin, you can buy a vocation promotion and become a royal paladin. ...

Go to a royalty such as Queen Eloise in Carlin or King Tibianus in Thais and donate 20.000 gold pieces to become promoted. Not only will you have a fancy new title, but also better regeneration and other advantages!
Choosing your vocation is a big step on your adventure, if not the biggest. It will change your life enormously, whether you become a knight, paladin, sorcerer or druid!
Spells, woah, that's a broad topic. Well, our most powerful spells are our holy spells which are especially effective against undead creatures. ...

We have also our own divine healing spell which is really useful once your level is high enough. We can also use some runes made by sorcerers and druids. Particularly area damage runes can save your butt in tight locations. ...
Then, we have ammunition creation spells. You can create your own arrows or bolts by using some of your mana. ...
This comes in handy when you're on a hunt and need something to spend your mana on... just create ammunition or food! ...

Well, he does not really like it if someone tells his story ... but I do! A long, long time ago Santa was nothing but a greedy little dwarf. A real miser, I tell ya ...
He was greedy even by dwarven standards. He would never share anything or give away the cheapest thing in his possession ...
One day a woman came to his house and asked him for a cup of water ...
Of course he refused. He even mocked her for being so naive. But what he did not know was that this woman was some kind of mighty fairy or perhaps a goddess in disguise ...
Be it as it may, the woman cursed old Santa, forcing him to share his fortune with everyone he met ...
Santa was horrified. Of course, he could not bear the thought of sharing anything at all. So he went into hiding ...
He hid in the most remote places in the world, but time and again someone found him out, and the curse made him share his wealth ...
And know something? Old santa actually came to like it! He saw the joy his presents brought, and this opened his old stony heart ...
And he learnt that this way his fortune gave him more joy and pleasure than it ever did when he locked it away. ...
Over the years he turned it into a game. He hid somewhere to reward those who found him ...
But once every year, on a very special day which happens to be his curse's anniversary, he goes out and brings presents to the people, and especially to the children ...
Well, that is his story ... Nah, that's not a tear in my eye. It's just the wind, you know.

He was a great mage but an even greater cook. His recipes and spells are priceless. Sadly, even if we succeed in breaking the defences of Cake Keep Isle, we will only manage to decipher a tiny fraction of his knowledge. ...
And still, we don't know what happened to Kullu. He retreated from our world to fully concentrate on his research on cooking recipes and spells. ...
He was some sweet tooth for all that we know. And for sure a genius when it comes to baking and magic. ...
His kitchen magic was that amazing, you could not tell where baking ended and magic started.
To be undisturbed, he placed his keep on an isle that existed on a planar instability which allowed him to phase the isle out of existence for most of the time. ...
Additionally he surrounded the isle with a sorcery of his invention that defied most attempts to reach it. ...
It took us quite a while to figure out that he'd never be able to weave a protection spell against something he loved so dearly like cakes and bakery wares. ...
So we came up with the idea of the bridge.

After a few failed attempts with gingerbread boats and the like, we figured out how to reach Cake Keep Isle. We used the very ingredients we could derive from his cake golem attacks to build a stable cake bridge to his isle.
Ah well, that's an .. uhm .. funny story. ...
You see, after the first expedition reached the isle, they took so long trying to find a way to Kullu's secrets that the isle began to vanish into the void while they were still there. ...
The entire time, they were harassed by Kullu's cake golem guardians of the keep. In the last minute, they cast emergency teleports to their home cities. ...
The good thing is it was not too late and all escaped. Well, the bad thing is their spells somehow reacted with the void-rift of that place, building astral tunnels from the void to said cities. ...

Now, whenever the isle manifests, the tunnels manifest as well. The ugly part is that through this one-way tunnels the cake golem army that was apparently sucked into the void has access to the cities and can raid them. ...
But they are not only an annoyance but also our greatest chance. Nasty but tasty little buggers. They can be troublesome but we need them for our bridge construction.
The golems that raid the cities supply us with two major materials that we need to build our bridge to Cake Keep Isle. ...
One component is the sugary mass that can be gained if you slay one of them. We use it as a kind of mortar. ...

The second part is a bit trickier to get. It is the raw cake material. It is kind of challenging to gain it. We built extraction machines that can drain the base material from the still animated corpses. ...
We placed one in each of the raided cities. You will have to lure the golems into the machines, to extract the material from them. ...
We need it to have a stable base material that is resilient against wind, weather and salt water.
We invented machines that can extract the essence of the cake golems. That is the part that gives them the stability to move and withstand damage and environmental hazards. ...
Well, actually we had them built by the dwarven technomancers. But it was us who figured out the basic principles! ...
However, whenever a cake golem gets into one of those machines, it gets disassembled in the blink of an eye and we get the enchanted base which we use to build our bridge.
Do you have some sugar for me? Please note that you can hand me all your sugar at once, if you want to.

Now once we've got enough ingredients to finish the bridge, we have to face another challenge. And that is the cake keep itself! Is is an almost impenetrable though edible fortress made completely out of cake! ...
The thing is, to reach his secrets we will have to eat the whole cake! This is easier said than done though as the cake regenerates itself periodically with the help of magic. ...
So we only have a few minutes to eat a whole layer of the cake, only then it will not regenerate but the upper layer will come down. So layer for layer we have to eat that cake. ...
It will take an army of hungry Tibians to eat them all in time. Even then things have to be somewhat coordinated. ...
People have to be brought here, wait for their turn to eat and of course stay hungry. Eating another layer might prove futile if you do not wait a few minutes for the hunger to return. ...
The good thing is that all people, big and small, can participate. ...

I guess the isle had a nice and flashy name in the past. But you know how people are. Someone started to call it the Cake Isle and I guess it is only a matter of time until this is shortened to CI. ...
People don't take their time anymore, not even for enjoyment.

I and my husband run this farm.

This is a very old island. It magically appears and disappears. Right now it has returned somehow! It's for sure worth a visit if you want to travel into Tibia's past.
