Greetings, Player! Why do you disturb me?
The elves are a curious lot. Even though they distrust humans, it's quite easy to steal from them. To scam them, however, is not that easy. ...
Elven laws are also very cruel. They might kill you for a minor occurrence or throw you into Hellgate.
Ankrahmun is great for business despite its cruel laws. It's far too tempting to get all those treasures into your fingers to let the opportunity pass.
We have hardly any business in Carlin. The laws are quite harsh and the city guard in the hands of an overzealous family which makes bribery complicated. ...
With the exception of some alcohol smuggle, there is little to be gained there. And even there you have to deal with nasty competitors.

A neat little town for business. A bit too far away for my taste, but as long as you don't mess it up, you can earn a living there. Still, the people there have an odd philosophy, so you might need to adjust your practices somewhat.
My job, uh... what should I say... well, no need to invent something, I guess. I'm the leader of the thieves guild.
My job, uh... what should I say... well, no need to invent something, I guess. I'm the leader of the thieves guild.

Edron is peaceful and many people there live in opulence. So now and then it might be profitable to pay Edron a visit. On the other hand, it's a rather small town and word about your trickeries might spread faster than you'd appreciate.
A backwater town, but useful as hiding place when you are wanted for something.
One dragon is as bad as the other.
You're already a member, silly.
You're already a member, silly.
The dwarfs aren't easy to deal with. Of course, they have many treasures. Still, dwarfs will hold a grudge against you for decades and they might dedicate their lives to hunt you. ...
If an operation in Kazordoon is not getting you a huge profit, it's wiser to leave it.

There are many opportunities in Liberty Bay. The poor are eager allies against the rich, and the latter are often VERY rich. Still, the laws are quite strict, and poor or not, the locals are somewhat suspicious towards strangers.
They call me Dorian.
Oswald? He lives near the crossroads.
The city is promising but still a bit underdeveloped. Give it some years to grow and then it's ripe for harvest. For now, we try not to disturb such profitable growth.
Too far away to bother about and not worth the travel. The few people that emigrated from Carlin are not wealthy, neither are the barbarians that live there. ...
Not to mention the violence with which they treat strangers that annoy them.
Isn't this a nasty little place? All that fools, the yelling, the backstabbing, the swindle. I just love it.
Venore can be a gold mine but if you aren't careful, you might end up dead in the swamp. There are people in Venore that don't like it if their terrain is trespassed. ...
If you steal from the wrong guys, you're dead. If you scam the wrong person, you're dead. If you leave an unfavourable impression on the wrong person, you're dead. ...
Well, I guess you got the idea.
Good bye, Player!
Hail, traveller and welcome! I can help you getting started, offer various services or you can assist me on my mission, what shall it be.

Besides all of the services I can provide, I am also on a mission I could need some help with. The cave near here could be just what an aspiring adventurer needs. There are also many fellow adventurers in Tibia, don't hesitate to ask them for help or even join forces with others to overcome the many perils of this world!
I offer what equipment is left from my fellow students for trade as well as banking services, teach spells and provide healing.
Certainly, surely you can make some use of this for a small obolus.
My name is Hector, pleased to meet you, traveller!
I am a philosopher from Thais, working both for king Tibianus as an advisor as well as mentoring new students of the Edron Academy. Which is also part of the reason why I'm here now.
It should be exactly HH:MM am by now.
Thais is the commercial and cultural centre of Tibia. There's a lot to see and do.
I've been teaching and lecturing at Edron's academy for decades. It's an honourable faculty with many bright and talented individuals such as my dear friend and colleague Spectulus.
A dear friend of mine who I have worked with many an hour on countless projects and experiments. He's quite the character, always busy but will grow on you over time.
King Tibianus is the righteous and wise ruler I have the honour of working as an advisor for.
A troubled mind but he is kind at heart. He would lose his head if it wasn't firmly attached, however.
A tall tale, some warriors are quite obsessed with it.
I took my vows to help any adventurer in need, including healing and other services.
I am fine. Thank you. There is a bit less work here than I had expected but I am sure we will have some intriguing discoveries just waiting for us.
My name is Lurik. Odd enough you ask though. People hardly do that nowadays. I feel as if my name was painted above my head or something.
I am the local contact of the explorer's society. I just love it to be at the frontier of all known lands.
At this remote spot, news are old news. Did you hear that quara attacked Liberty Bay?

Maybe you already heard that we send our dead with a boat on their last journey. A rumour came to my ear that many of the corpses stranded on the small island of Helheim where they walk around as UNDEADS. I wonder if this is true.

This city has seen much in the few days of its existence. At first it was a little trading spot where ships form Carlin landed. Later it became a deposit for ore that has been mined in the mountains ...
Then local people joined the traders from Carlin and supplied them with fish, furs and meat ...
Soon it became a small settlement and the locals, fascinated with the abundance of wood the traders brought with them, begun to build houses ...
It became a centre of conflict when some barbarians decided it was wrong to settle in a town and later on struggled to survive when the contact to Carlin was lost for decades ...
Today, the city got a little boost by the presence of foreigners here. But only the future will tell what the fate of this city will be.
Our noble society is dedicated to explore the unknown. No location is too remote for our members to travel there ...
No beast is too wild to be hunted. No treasure buried too deep to be unearthed ...
Only the most dedicated and fearless adventurers may join our ranks.
Currently we maintain public bases in Port Hope and Northport. We have also established this humble outpost here.
But you are already a member, Player.
You are an explorer of the explorer's society.
You have been awarded the sea scout badge.
I currently have no further missions for you, my friend. But you may use the astral portal in the upper room from now on. ...
For just one orichalcum pearl, you can travel between Liberty Bay and Svargrond.

There are several tradesmen here in the city. However, with the exception of the traders of the Carlin consortium, they are unlikely to trade with you until you have proven yourself as worthy. Best you asked the jarl about the barbarian test.
Everspring is the realm of the dead. It is a place of peace and harmony where those who boldly braved the challenges of life dwell for eternity and share stories at the campfires after a hunt ...
Every true barbarian that is properly brought into afterlife will join the great hunt in Everspring where the animals are fat and have the thickest furs.
Those barbarian who did oppose the building of this settlements call themselves raiders. They consist of some major and minor clans. ...
It's said that they are lead by a shaman woman, who has celebrated her 100th birthday a long time ago, but I am not sure how believable such records are.
An honourary barbarian earns the right to become a citizen here. But to prove yourself worthy, you have to pass the barbarian test.
We heard that this mythical dwarf lives somewhere on the southern Ice Islands.
The dragons on our isles have adapted to the climate as every creature here. Instead of being aligned to fire, they became creatures of the cold ...
They are fierce and dangerous but, luckily, they only prey on beasts of the sea or those that wander the ice near their lairs.

The yetis are mythical beasts. Only few that encountered those creatures lived to tell the tale. The chakoyas worship them as divine beings, although they have no real relations to them, as far as we can tell.
It's a shame I still have not seen a living chakoya. I could examine some dead specimen though and I have seen some of their victims ...
It's hard to believe that such a small creature is such a terrible threat but for all I can tell they are indeed quite dangerous.
Some time ago, a few elves came here but they could not stand the cold and so they left pretty soon. Most likely it was Nibelor in which they have been interested.

I met some of those little people in the past. Considering our experience with the chakoyas, we don't underestimate someone just for its look. And those dwarfs proved indeed to be powerful, courageous and enduring.
There are many dangerous creatures that roam our isles. But having seen what men can do to each other, I wouldn't call any of them a monster.
This is a dangerous, unforgiving land. If you leave the city, you will have to deal with creatures that survive in this harsh environment. They are for sure a challenge for the unwary.
We understand that our friends from Carlin are wary with the realm ruled by Thais but this is not of our concern.
We are friends of the Carliners. Still we don't allow their politics to influence our way to handle things here.
We did not allow them to stay here. This had nothing to do with our friendship with Carlin but for the way they handled things and their harmful approach to go hunting.
We have heard only little about this far away place.
We have heard only little about this far away place.
The raiders' camps are mainly located in the south-western part of the isle. The camps are named after the major clans of the raiders: Ragnir, Bittermor and Grimhorn.
Nibelor has always been a sacred place for our people. The druids and shamans live there.
The people here seem to be a bit uncivilised on the first glance. Rest rest assured that they are hospitable and generous if you earn their respect in some way.
The jarl is a kind of chieftain of the local people here. If you haven't done yet, talk to him. If you want to be accepted by the people here, you will have to ask the jarl for the barbarian test.

No kings or queens rule these remote lands.
No kings or queens rule these remote lands.

Most shaman and druids of our people live on the sacred isle Nibelor. There, they divine the future, calm the wrath of father Chyll and prepare the dead for their last travel to the lands of Everspring.

Most shaman and druids of our people live on the sacred isle Nibelor. There, they divine the future, calm the wrath of father Chyll and prepare the dead for their last travel to the lands of Everspring.
I don't care what people who come here believe in. If they provoke father Chyll, he will take care of them on his own. If their gods prove to be more powerful than Chyll, they might deserve to live.
A long time ago when the trade with Carlin was flourishing, people actually worked in the mines. During the years of the serpents, the mines had been abandoned. ...
Later, the raiders took shelter there, although they blame us for living in a fortified city ...
Now, the traders of Carlin are back but some other foreigners seem to have claimed the mines from the raiders ...

It's neither our business nor would we have the manpower to help them to recapture the mines. Also, if they do not have the strength to get the mines back on their own, they don't deserve them anyway.
Father north wind is called Chyll by our people. He is an unforgiving hunter. He knows no mercy with the weak ...
Chyll is a harsh god and the best you can do is to avoid his attention. Only the shamans and druids deal with him.
It was an astonishing phenomenon. For decades, sea serpents made it impossible to reach these northern isles by ship ...
The most puzzling part of this event is probably the fact that sea serpents usually prefer a southern climate ...
However, almost over night the sea serpents seemed to be gone and the contact between Carlin and the isles here could finally be reestablished.
We know of father Chyll and his freezing breath. We care little for other gods. It is foolish to meddle with beings that are so powerful ...
We leave it to the druids and shamans to handle such affairs.
It's some dark side of mythical powers. Such things should only be dealt with by druids or shamans.
It's some light side of mythical powers. Such things should only be dealt with by druids or shamans.
He's a warrior god as far as I understood it. Well, in the end you have to fight your battles by yourself and not some mystic entity.
Even here we heard about this powerful man. Travellers from the south only dare to whisper his name.
On the campfire, there are numerous tales about this weapon. It's told that it has been missing since ages ...
In my opinion, the power and fame of a weapon shouldn't exceed the power and fame of it's wielder. And I have not heard of any hero whose fame would surpass that of excalibug.
Good bye. Come back soon with exciting stories about your travels.
Ah, the freedom of travelling.
Be greeted, child Player. I welcome you.
Ah, you want to replace your adventurer's stone for free?

This Charlotta has an evil influence on the population. Too many listen to her or are intimidated by her. I've asked the guards to stop her for her own good. But there is nothing they can do unless she openly commits some sort of crime.
In the past he used to be a charming agitator, still people feared his might and his magic. ...

His leadership came to an end when the Thaians arrived. That was the end of his schemes to achieve more power. He is still out there somewhere and, once again, he tries to persuade people of his evil plans with the help of lies and intimidation.
A cult? Are you serious? You probably refer to the web of fear and superstition that the old Chondur has created.
What a lovely young lady. I am sure more than one man has a crush on her. Only time will tell whom she might choose.
Although they might follow a noble goal, they should never forget that some things are not meant to be known by mere mortals.
Of course he had sunken low before he became an incarnation of evil. On the other hand, he is an example that a mere human can leave the boundaries of his mortal shell with the help of the gods. ...
Therefore, he should not only strike people with awe but also inspire the wish to strive for a better life-form.
A kind man that always gives his share to the temple. Of course people still criticise him but most of them are old natives that still bear a grudge against Thais and Venore.
She visits the temple now and then to pray silently but rarely attends the messes. Of course it is not up to me to judge such behaviour.

It is sad that the king is so far away. Without his guidance, things sometimes just don't work out as well as they could. Also people say that others might have too much influence on decisions. This is of course not the king's fault.
The city is still young and growing. With the help of the higher powers it will prosper for sure.
You do not need any healing right now.
You do not need any healing right now.

Mr. Loveless is a cultivated man that understands the principles of trade and diplomacy like no one else. In spite of all obstacles Venore might have here, he manages to organise festivities for the important families of the town.

Oh my, pirates and other types of criminals are always an unwelcome companion to culture. But there are always some people that the twists of life have driven into black despair that ended up in a life of a criminal.
I guess whoever controls the plantations, also controls the isle.

The quara are a dire threat. They should never ever be underestimated. We have no idea what they are up to. I doubt that military strength alone can help us when the day should come on which they launch the final attack on us.
He is one of the leaders of these murderous pirates.
Rum is a treacherous and dangerous lover.
Sugar is important for the isles. It is pure gold in the right hands.
Thais and Liberty Bay are quite different. We have our own problems, and we will have to find our own solutions.
That young man always appears a bit absent. He seems not to focus his thoughts on what he is doing. I wonder if that young man does not have too many responsibilities.
I am a humble priest. Healer for the wounded and guide to those who lost their path.
I am a humble priest. Healer for the wounded and guide to those who lost their path.
Venore is a wealthy city of trade and commerce. Some people consider its influence here as a problem. I am not good in politics and I have no real opinion on this matter.

A futile attempt of some local magicians to use little tricks and superstition in their favour. However, true power is not acquired so easily. True command of the spirits is not achieved by old hags in ramshackle huts, fumbling with some dolls.
Such a fine man. I admire his patience considering all those petty problems he has to handle constantly.

There are five blessings available in five sacred places: the spiritual shielding, the spark of the phoenix, the embrace of Tibia, the fire of the suns and the wisdom of solitude. Additionally, you can receive the twist of fate here. ...
There are also two enhanced blessings for further reduction of experience loss.
I can sense that the druids north of Carlin have provided you with the Embrace of Tibia.

It is said that one enhanced blessing, the 'heart of the mountain', has been lost in the icy wastes of Svargrond. Find a nomad far to the west of these barren lands, hiding in the cold there, slightly above ground. ...

It is also said that a mysterious djinn, bound to an existence of slavery, lies buried somewhere beneath the northern Tiquanda jungle. I cannot confirm whether this tale is true but if you find him, you shall also find the 'blood of the mountain'.
I can see you received the blessing of the two suns in the suntower near Ab'Dendriel.
I can see you received the blessing of the two suns in the suntower near Ab'Dendriel.

Whenever you receive a lethal wound, your vital force is damaged and there is a chance that you lose some of your equipment. With every single of the five blessings you have, this damage and chance of loss will be reduced.

I can sense that the spark of the phoenix already was given to you by the dwarven priests of earth and fire in Kazordoon.

I see you received the spiritual shielding in the whiteflower temple south of Thais.

This is a special blessing I can bestow upon you once you have obtained at least one of the other blessings and which functions a bit differently. ...
It only works when you're killed by other adventurers, which means that at least forty percent of the damage leading to your death was caused by others, not by monsters or the environment. ...

The twist of fate will not reduce the death penalty like the other blessings, but instead prevent you from losing your other blessings as well as the amulet of loss, should you wear one. It costs the same as the other blessings. ...
Would you like to receive that protection for a sacrifice of 50000 gold, child?

Our army is well prepared and supported by our Venorean friends whenever needed.
I am the representative of his royal highness, the King of Thais. It is my responsibility to keep things here in Liberty Bay going, so to speak.

I am sure the king will call Carlin back into the Thaian empire as soon as possible. If only those women weren't so stubborn.
That old hag cannot be trusted. I am quite sure that it is her who is responsible for much of the unrest among the people in town ...
There are no positive proofs but I ordered the guards to be wary about things that concern her.
Theodore Loveless really knows how to run a party. I entrust those matters to him entirely.
Nonsense! I do not want to hear these old women's tales again! Although some sinister cult would perfectly fit those natives here, there IS no such a thing as a secret cult.
The society has full support of our beloved king and so I do my best to further their causes ...
Personally I think a nobleman can do better things with their times but at least they let the dirty work be done by some adventurers.
These lies that tell about him living here in the past are nothing but tavern tales.

The king is a wise man with a noble spirit. I will not allow this colony to fail in his eyes.

A man of style and wisdom. An incarnation of the old values. I would like to add that he and me share the same ideals and the way to view things. He is of immense help in my efforts to bring civilisation to the colonies.

The sorceress of Edron academy stays on her own. I appreciate that - a mage interfering with our internal affairs would be the last thing we need. Of course as a representative of the Edron academy she has my full support.
I am too old to care about fairy tales.

Bah, this is the true ugly face of these so-called freedom fighters. Murder and plunder is all they care about. But we will rout these cowardly criminals out and soon they will be nothing more than a footnote in history.
I agree to Mr. Loveless' point of view: We could produce more if the workers were not that lazy.
That backwater town still has no governor. I can't blame anyone that he doesn't want to end up there.
